:::{#cor-gamma-variance}
#### Variance of the gamma distribution

If $T \sim \dGamf{\shape, \rate}$,
then $\Var{T} = \shape / \rate^2$.

:::

::: proof

First, the second moment, by @thm-gamma-moments with $k = 2$:

$$
\ba
\E{T^2}
&= \frac{\gammafn(\shape + 2)}{\gammafn(\shape) \, \rate^2}
&& (\text{moment formula with } k = 2) \\
&= \frac{(\shape + 1) \, \gammafn(\shape + 1)}{\gammafn(\shape) \, \rate^2}
&& (\gammafn(\shape + 2) = (\shape + 1) \, \gammafn(\shape + 1)) \\
&= \frac{(\shape + 1) \, \shape \, \gammafn(\shape)}{\gammafn(\shape) \, \rate^2}
&& (\gammafn(\shape + 1) = \shape \, \gammafn(\shape)) \\
&= \frac{\shape (\shape + 1)}{\rate^2}
&& (\text{cancel } \gammafn(\shape))
\ea
$$

Then, by the [simplified expression for variance](variance-covariance.qmd#thm-variance) and @cor-gamma-mean:

$$
\ba
\Var{T}
&= \E{T^2} - \sqf{\E{T}}
&& (\text{simplified expression for variance}) \\
&= \frac{\shape (\shape + 1)}{\rate^2} - \frac{\shape^2}{\rate^2}
&& (\text{mean of the gamma distribution}) \\
&= \frac{\shape^2 + \shape - \shape^2}{\rate^2}
&& (\text{expand } \shape (\shape + 1) \text{ and combine fractions}) \\
&= \frac{\shape}{\rate^2}
&& (\shape^2 - \shape^2 = 0)
\ea
$$

:::
